**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Block publication when legacy media remains**

When `MEDIA_STRATEGY` is `D1_BLOB` and a submitted listing still contains a preserved `listing_images` row with `blob_data IS NULL`, this update publishes it without the legacy-media guard used by the owner and public endpoints. The admin queue also omits that row, so an admin can unknowingly publish the listing; afterward `/public/listings` returns `LEGACY_MEDIA_MIGRATION_REQUIRED` for the entire catalog page containing it. Check `hasLegacyD1Images` before approval/publication and fail closed until migration is complete.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the admin destination after session expiry**

When an admin's session expires while using this new route, `setSessionExpiredHandler` still redirects to login with `redirect=/owner`. After the admin signs in, `AuthView` honors that redirect, and the OWNER-only route guard then sends the admin to `/`, so reauthentication loses the moderation workflow instead of returning to `/admin`. Make the expiry redirect retain the current protected route or select a role-appropriate destination.

Addressed in ccec80df4f273fee36dc4921b1af00b13c19ae36. The ADMIN review queue now explicitly flags preserved D1_BLOB rows with NULL blob_data, and both approval and publication fail closed with 409 LEGACY_MEDIA_MIGRATION_REQUIRED while such a row exists. Added a regression that checks queue visibility, both responses, and unchanged SUBMITTED/UNPUBLISHED state; focused Worker suite passes 15/15.

Addressed in ccec80df4f273fee36dc4921b1af00b13c19ae36. Session expiry now preserves the current protected destination (including /admin), falling back to /owner only when the current route is public. The Playwright ADMIN E2E clears the cookie, calls the protected queue endpoint, verifies login?redirect=/admin, then reauthenticates back to the review screen; the full local ADMIN flow passes 9/9.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Run the admin moderation suite in CI**

Adding `admin-moderation.test.ts` to Vitest's `include` list does not make the repository's checks execute it: `apps/worker/package.json` has no admin test script, and the worker job in `.github/workflows/quick-checks.yml` invokes only the catalog, media, owner, and preview-auth scripts, each with explicit test filenames. Consequently, regressions in the new ADMIN authorization and atomic review/audit transitions can merge while all required checks remain green; add this suite to an invoked script or workflow step.

Fixed in d1bde27e82b7fe25f1896a740d849735f0b2440b: added the `test:admin` npm script and a worker-job step in `.github/workflows/quick-checks.yml`. Local `npm run test:admin` passes 4/4 and Worker typecheck passes. The required worker check is running on this exact PR head and now invokes the ADMIN suite; I will resolve this thread after that check passes.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Index the global audit ordering**

When the new admin view loads or refreshes, it calls `/admin/listings/audit?limit=30` without a `listingId`, and that endpoint orders the entire table by `created_at DESC, id DESC`. This index starts with `listing_id`, so SQLite cannot use it for that global ordering and must scan and sort the growing audit history before applying the limit; the moderation page will therefore become progressively slower and more expensive. Add an index led by `created_at` (with `id` as the tie-breaker), especially since the pinned source mapping records multiple audit indexes that this parity-first migration currently reduces to one.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the Preview configuration fail-closed check to ADMIN**

When an Access Preview is missing or has invalid Access configuration while a previously issued ADMIN JWT remains valid, these new routes still accept that token because the global `previewAuthConfigured` gate matches only `/auth` and `/listings`. OWNER operations fail with 503 in the same configuration, but ADMIN review and publication can continue; include `/admin` in that Preview-auth availability gate before this middleware authenticates the session.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the source audit record shape**

When existing source `AdminAuditLog` rows are migrated—or later ADMIN actions audit entities other than listings—this table cannot represent the documented source contract in `apps/worker/docs/postgres-d1-map.md:11`: it omits `entityType`, nullable `entityId`, and JSON `metadata`, while making `listingId` and `targetOwnerId` mandatory. That forces migration code to discard or coerce audit history and prevents generic ADMIN events from being recorded; mirror the source nullability and structured metadata, including JSON validation, before treating this as the ADMIN audit migration.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Index the moderation queue ordering**

With migrations 0001–0008 applied, SQLite reports `SCAN l` and `USE TEMP B-TREE FOR ORDER BY` for this exact queue query because no index supports the pending-state predicate followed by `created_at DESC, id DESC`. Thus every initial refresh and every cursor page scans and sorts the growing listings table before returning at most 101 rows, negating the scalability benefit of the new pagination and increasing D1 rows read; add an index/query shape that supports this moderation ordering.

Migration copies prior synthetic listing events and rejection reason into JSON metadata.
